notes.title: [Beta] 2017.07.29 - Shader Changes
notes.notes:
First off: this isn't the beta you're looking for. Many of you have been patiently awaiting the big beta overhaul, and while this is a beta release, it is just the standard build with a couple of potentially volatile items that I need tested.

This update contains changes to the launcher and primary fragment shader, which are two things that can cause a lot of unforseen headaches on different OS and hardware setups, necessitating a beta release before pushing these changes out to everyone. You can opt to receive beta releases at any time by looking for the betas tab of the game's properties in your Steam library.

So why am I pushing these volatile changes out now instead of holding them for the big beta? This shader change aims to address one of the more common complaints I've seen: why does the game have to look so retro? I get it, you like pixels, but these ones are too big, or the pixelated fonts can be hard on your eyes, or you're just not in the mood to have sharp, saturated blocks of color pumped into your retinas. I've done things in the past to assist with this: various filters and the "double-res" fonts, but it seems nothing has quite done the trick!

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7608706/eae898ecf59d2e3ffa67f69a1402f987796e3725.png

So I'm introducing new "smooth" and "artsy" pixel filters (leftmost section of images is "hard" pixels). The "smooth" setting is replacing the default "soft" pixel setting (which was virtually indistinguishable from "hard" at most standard resolutions), while the old, rubbish "artsy" filter has been completely discarded in favor of a much smarter smoothing algorithm of my own design (I had a great vacation this year!).

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7608706/6f5af6cd60f708f4e966df376a14a42edc2a0487.png

The "smooth" filter intelligently rounds the corners of non-contiguous pixels to create a subtle softness without compromising sharp pixel edges. It even helps improve the double-res fonts:

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7608706/b468ff9b53df72b5202a970ecdda22a0c5fdcea5.png

The old "artsy" filter was a poor attempt to disguise the game's pixels, but it ended up a mess; the new version, on the other hand, is very playable. However, the double-res fonts are not usable with this filter (it makes them look worse, while the low-res fonts actually look quite smooth and legible).

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7608706/e82484b22ae72fd5afbef8e69978e25eb77752e1.gif

Other changes: the double-resolution fonts are now the default, and the launcher no longer keeps a console window open while you're playing (an inadvertent side-effect to launcher fixes from this past spring).

Changing the default shader and font set is a significant design change for me, as most of the game was developed to adhere very strictly to the grid (no rotating, scaling, or offsetting pixels), and compromises were available but never pushed in the past. Development on the beta has me re-evaluating a lot of priorities, though, and I need to offer the best default experience I can. Please let me know whether you feel this is a step in the right direction, and of course, please report any issues you have with this release so I can prepare the standard release quickly.

Thank again, everyone!

Changelog
Changes:
"Artsy" filter is completely different, no longer sucky
"Soft" filter (the default setting) replaced with "Smooth" filter with slightly rounded corners
Double-res font set is now enabled by default (for new players)
On Windows, launcher no longer leaves a console window open while the game is running

notes.title: Beta Progress Update - Inventory
notes.notes:
I am sorry to say that I still do not have a beta release date in sight, but I feel I owe you all some insight into the changes you can expect when it arrives.

First off, for those who are unaware, my last few months have been spent working on some massive changes to the game's mechanics which I will eventually release in a beta form, for additional workshopping. Progress has been slow on account of this now being a part-time gig for me along with having had a new child recently, but I am trying to make more time available. My relative silence is mostly due to difficulty justifying talking over working, but I really do want to keep you all in the loop, so it's about time I share some more.

My general goals for this beta period are to:
Reduce the number of core mechanics and types of interaction
Increase the clarity and depth of remaining mechanics
Introduce end-game content and victory scenarios
Emphasize an escalation in complexity over time


This post will be focusing on the first couple of points, but I want to make it clear that while some of this may sound like "dumbing down" the game, this beta is really about growing the game's scalability (and enjoyability) from casual to core. The aim is to achieve this by distilling the early game into fewer essential elements--so it is more approachable and well-defined--, and then ramp up the complexity and interplay of those elements through the unlocked content (increased minion synergy, advanced items, and layered late-game rules).

Possibly the largest mechanical change going into the introductory beta release is the removal of the traditional inventory and refactoring of item functionality. In the beta, you will no longer have a ten-slot inventory of passive and usable items; instead, each resource will now have an assigned item--chosen before the game starts--, and these items will relate more directly to their associated resource.

In conjunction, the current resource-specific matching bonuses are being removed. These are the effects inherent to each resource--like healing when matching Flesh--, which were introduced to give resource-matching a little more weight beyond buying things.

At face value, these changes may sound alarming, but here's my reasoning:

The game's inventory and item mechanics went through a lot of iterations before settling where they are today, but most items currently fall into one of two categories: static items that give you a bonus in exchange for an inventory slot, and usable items that you have to remember to click every so often. I suppose this system works fine, but neither of these options are really engaging; many of the usable items encourage immediate re-use over careful planning, and the passives are essentially a trade-off that keep you from having another usable.

The matching bonuses were poorly explained and easily ignored; by design, they were rewarding even for players who did not pay attention to them, but that didn't make them feel relevant. Even if you did pay attention to them, it was easy to dismiss the resource effects you didn't care for. It was all about saving those Bone matches, right?

The resource/item changes are designed to address these shortfalls, while maintaining the benefits of both mechanics. At the start of a game, you will be able to swap freely between any unlocked item (between games, the hoard area has been changed to offer options for this and banner selection), with each item retaining the level it was last at, so you can level each item across multiple games, then trade it out for a round without feeling punished for trying something new.

Each item is now tied to its resource in a deliberate fashion, and currently, they fall into five basic categories (category names are, as any of this, subject to change): Artifacts, Contingencies, Potions, Conduits, and Modifiers.

Most of the game's passive items are becoming Artifacts and Contingencies; these are passive categories, but with a minimum or maximum required resource threshold, respectively. For example, the holy damage reduction from the Helm only remains in effect so long as you maintain an indicated level of the Gear resource. On the other hand, the Punji contingency now offers a bonus trap on all trap floors whenever the Growth resource is low.

The previously usable Potions now function similarly to the past matching bonuses; the item's effect is activated per every so many points of the target resource. The key difference is that partial progress toward the next activation carries between moves. For example, the new Lazarus Lotion requires (currently) 10 Bone to activate, resurrecting a minion for free; this is steeper than the old bone-matching bonus, but it can be activated across multiple matches. (If you are concerned about timing the larger quantity to coincide with the loss of a minion, check the miscellaneous updates below for a relevant change to resurrections).

Conduits are similar to Potions, but offer a bigger bonus that require larger single matches to activate; progress does not carry across moves, and while a potion can be triggered multiple times in a single move, the conduit's effect is detonated once per move. When gathering a large quantity of Ruin, the Balding Bomb now detonates any remaining Ruin tiles (explosion size scaling with Bomb level), gathering neighboring tiles and building upon the current move's multiplier.

Finally, we have Modifiers, which create different Hoard matching behaviors when grabbing tiles of the same color. The Magnet, for instance, will now cause all Scrap drags to have a range within which Gear matches with Scrap; the Gear will gain an orange Scrap background, but be collected as Gear--of course, the increased multiplier will also benefit any Scrap gathered. These items are generally the most experimental, but everything here is subject to change based on how the beta plays.

So there are more types of items than before, but I've removed several forms of interaction (clicking usables, managing inventory items, selling items, etc.), and these new mechanics don't rely upon any new interactions. Aside from possibly some Modifiers, none of these effects strictly require player knowledge, either; they are bonuses that can simply occur through standard play, but the new model should reward strategy far more than before and allow players to better customize the mechanics to match their playstyle. The thresholds will also make it easier to balance passive items--I am aware that there are some rather OP items in the current release...

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7608706/58f547d948d3f0c74bc66db6108121be1f5912b6.png

This is the WIP Hoard with composite sample resource bars taken from multiple sessions--I thought you all may be able to chime in on your preferred layout for the min, max, and resource icons. The first six bars use a 30-pixel height to represent any maximum; notice how the 17 Growth appears higher than the 20 Gear. The last two resources use a different bar with a 1:1 pixel:unit height, where the total max possible is 40 but the meter's level is a truer representation of its value. I am leaning toward that sizing, but I'd like to have others weigh in. The entire Hoard frame and background should be receiving a facelift, as well, but I can't really work on styling things until these other decisions are settled.

I would also love to hear your thoughts on which items should become the new default for each resource. I am thinking the four pillar Potions (Cordial, Quaff, Adamantiserum, and Magi-jack), a couple of Contingencies and a couple of Conduits, but I am not sure.

Other things you may notice about this image: the rituals are missing and the moving tile queue is gone. The rituals were temporarily removed from this build, because I have been experimenting with reserving them for another mechanic; this is not likely to be in the initial beta release, so you can probably expect those to appear on the edges, as before. However, the moving tile queue that catches falling tiles and reserves cleared rows is out, because in this build, I have removed the clearance requirement for new floors. You'll be able to build any floor you can afford without clearing room, and there will instead be an overall space constraint that increases with the wave count (this rule will itself change later in the beta).

There are a lot of other things going on, too; here are some of the other changes slated for the initial beta release:
All characters are receiving stat and ability revisions
No more resurrection time limit on minions; minions always resurrect to their previous selves (so long as they are not dead when the dungeon crumbles), but this means minion purchase prices go steadily up as the game progresses and your minions increase in level
Heroes no longer build checkpoints but instead establish them on undefended floors
Floors are "fortified" by placing three defenders on them; each floor bestows a different bonus when fortified
About a dozen new items to build variety

And there are many other changes (and additions!) planned for this extended beta period. It is just going to take longer to get there than I had expected.

Of course, throughout all of this, the standard release will remain the standard release. The beta is open to all, but requires an opt-in from the game's properties in your Steam library; you can actually opt-in right now to receive the beta branch as soon as it goes live, and it will replace the standard release in your library.

Please let me know what you all think, either here in the comments, or over on the thread I've set up for more in-depth discussion. Thank you again for all of your ideas and patience :totcordial: !

notes.title: 2016.05.27: Merged Beta Changes!
notes.notes:
After five months of a split release favoring an opt-in beta branch, I am finally merging the releases, confirming all of the huge beta changes and additions that many of you have helped test and shape over those months. I am so thankful for all of your insight and reports that aided me in directing development over this time, and I look forward to working with all of you on similar major additions in the future.

But first, I want to spend the next few weeks focusing on polish and bug fixes, to ensure that the standard release has regained the stability that allowed the previous major release to stand alone for so many months. There will be other minor additions and content, too, but no huge new features for a little while. I do still have more of that planned, though =).

If you haven't been following along with the beta releases, there may be some shock when you load up this build, but almost everything about the beta changes was designed to improve the user experience, so don't be intimidated if things look a little different. To make things easier, the changelog below is a bit more on the abridged side than usual--just brass tacks.

New to this release versus the previous beta release (a week ago) is an enforced camera fixation on the Sanctum when your Tyrant is in danger (and a slight slow-motion effect), and a brief "epilogue" following your Tyrant's demise (there will probably be some more expansion upon this in the future).

I anticipate several minor follow-up releases over the next couple of days, to address any major bug reports; please report anything out of place--either on the forum, or to me directly (you are all cordially invited to send me a friend request at any time!)! Thank you again for all of the support over the beta months; I hope you all enjoy the end result as much as I do! :totcordial:

Changelog
New and Different Stuff:
Fresh leaderboards for high score and plots completed. These aspects of the game have changed too much, and I'm sorry for the inconvenient reset. I have kept the old leaderboards available to the community for posterity, though, and now the worst item on the list is out of the way!
The Hoard is now always visible on the left
All minions can be dragged/dropped; portraits for all characters are now over on the right
Generally lower minion and hero counts; everyone is named, and everyone feels more important and more manageable.
Combat has been overhauled to be 3v3 without position shuffling; there is less guesswork when it comes to minion placement.
Characters heal slightly after they have been targetted, at the same point where they draw fatigue.
No more "deployable" items--only usables and passives.
Items can be leveled up by collecting duplicates in subsequent playthroughs.
Early hero checkpoints now gain portals that allow heroes to teleport into your dungeon directly.
No more legacy points; instead:

All items carry over
Resource caps carry over -5 (never dropping below the base cap)
Floors are "fortified" by completing plots; fortified floors survive destruction
For each fortified floor, one of your highest ranking minions will survive destruction (the chosen minions' portraits will be marked in orange).

All minions level up by gaining experience; 10 levels.
Recently slain minions can be bought back from the dead (all experience in-tact) at an increased price
New corruption mechanic for turning heroes to your side
Removed the score multiplier
Removed casual mode
Added cloud saving support
Added controller support
Several achievement goals have been slightly adjusted
Matches grant simple resource-determined bonuses to your characters; for example, flesh matches now heal minions. Sometimes, it is now beneficial to save a match for a time when your minions will need it.
There are a couple of new Hoard elements: dirt blocks, and anchor stones. There is the potential to add a few more things in this vein down the road.
Major change to messagelog layout
Lots of UI changes and improvements
Five or six new floors and other such stuff
Plenty of other stuff that I've either forgotten to mention or felt wasn't super important.

notes.title: 2015.07.28: Changes and Fixes
notes.notes:
I am newly returned from an Internet-light family reunion with a bunch of changes and fixes. Apologies if I've been a bit slower to respond to posts, comments, screenshots, reviews, etc. lately; as though a wi-fi diet were insufficiently Luddite, the great outdoors saw fit to destroy my phone, as well.

It was a good--if somewhat unproductive--trip, though, and I look forward to resuming regular updates! notes.title: [Beta] 2015.07.06: Incoming Mechanical Changes
notes.notes:
[Due to major mechanical changes, this is a beta release; you can opt in to the beta by opening the game's Properties from your Steam Library, and browsing to the "Betas" tab. Many Steam features are disabled in this release, but I would greatly appreciate any comments and suggestions you wonderful testers are able to provide. I aim to push this out to everyone within the week. It's also worth noting that if you opt to receive beta releases, you will also receive normal releases when the beta becomes obsolete.]

I received a lot of excellent feedback over the first week of regular release, and I am now translating it into new and revised mechanics; there are a couple of big changes here, and even more on the way in the next couple of days. I am aiming to simplify some mechanics to make the game more approachable while also bolstering the challenge for veteran players (hopefully without harming the novice experience).

Drag/Drop Any Minion Instantly
Firstly, you can now drag and drop any minion (not just champions) on to any valid floor to immediately move them. This allows you to more quickly build encounters or substitute one minion in for another mid-combat.

If you want a minion to stay on a floor that you drop them on (similar to the previous "stationing" mechanic, they will either need to be dropped into combat or that floor will need to be set to "Defend." Minions no longer take turns playing defense on "Defended" floors; they should generally waste less time.

The goal with this change is to bring more strategy to the dungeon management and make it much simpler than before: no more followers, and no more special rules for champions. Everyone is drag and drop, and everything is quicker and cleaner.

Checkpoint Floors
The other major addition with this update are "checkpoint floors," which are special floors that automatically appear every 5th floor. These are off-limits, hero-built floors, which you have no control over.

When heroes reach these floors, they will camp for the remainder of the wave, much as they do on the surface, and when the next wave begins, they will continue their descent. Heroes that make it to these floors will be instantly healed, un-poisoned, fearless, etc., and will also level up.

These floors should help divide your dungeon into multiple fronts, which can be a blessing for weaker dungeons, while also keeping the threat fresh for stronger dungeons.

Other Stuff
Previously, minions would recover defense immediately after leaving combat, but that poses problems when you are able to simply drag them out and then back into the fight. Now, all characters (minions and heroes) regenerate defense and even health (if defense is full) while out of combat, at a rate of about one point every fifteen seconds. 

These changes (and the other upcoming ones) will require some revisions to the tutorial and general help topics, which have not been made yet, so keep in mind that there may still be erroneous references to followers and such.

I have some new content prepared, but I've been too busy testing and tweaking mechanics to try out the new stuff, so it's been held back. I know I said bonus content this time around, but I think it may have to wait until after this beta release has been thoroughly tested. Sorry for the delay on that!

Changelog
Additions:
Checkpoint Floor: Challenging Checkpoint (actually has randomized names, as multiple can exist in a single dungeon)
Changes:
All minions can now be instantly dragged and dropped on to other floors
Minions can be tagged in and out of battles using this system
Many small changes to minion patrolling AI
All characters now regenerate fatigue and health over time when not in combat (currently, about one point every 15 seconds)
Can no longer tell a champion to flee by clicking their battle icon (simplifying a mechanic that isn't strictly necessary and which many players didn't realize existed--you can instead drop the champ elsewhere and instantly remove them from a battle)
Characters can be dropped on champion portraits to move them to the champion's floor or to send them pillaging (if that champion is pillaging and the dragged character is also a champion)
Removed follower mechanics
Removed "Throw [x] a Party!" plot (no longer possible)
Fleeing heroes can regroup at checkpoints (they will not level up again, however)

Fixes:
Fixed a crash involving dragging/clicking floors, minions, or heroes in specific situations
Fixed a crash related to scared heroes in certain combat positions
Fixed a couple of incorrect sound effects
Legacy items could load into different inventory slots than they were saved in

notes.title: 2015.06.25: Standard Release
notes.notes:
This is the game's first standard release. I am transitioning out of beta and Early Access and into the, well, not "full" or "complete" release, because I expect to greatly expand the game's content over the coming months, but I think "standard" release is an okay term. Just because we're exiting Early Access doesn't mean I'm done listening to your feedback; the game wouldn't be what it is now without all of your opinions, suggestions, bug reports, and support, so thank you ːtotcordialː! Please continue telling me what you enjoy, what you'd like to see more of, and what needs work!

Also, please consider taking and posting a screenshot of the game to help me update the storefront and increase the diversity of images presented there; I'm offering sponsorship credits!

notes.title: Update 2015.04.27c: Re-Balancing
notes.notes:
I was pretty happy with where the game's balance had been sitting prior to this week's major changes; it wasn't where I eventually want it to be, but then, the game hasn't quite evolved to a state that would support what I'd like just yet.

The big matching/item/pause changes greatly affected the game's overall balance, even more so than I was anticipating; I knew scores would escalate due to both the multiplier as well as the increased survivability that comes with infinitely re-usable items and more readily available resources, but I wasn't quite prepared for just how much easier the game would end up being. So now you can all expect slight adjustments here and there until I am once again satisfied with where the balance stands.

Thank you to everyone who discussed how they felt about the new mechanics and balance, and those who posted screenshots and scores which I could use as references for these tweaks. I look forward to seeing how everyone feels about these and future changes =).

There were actually three updates today, thus the "c" in the version number; here's what's been changed or fixed.

Changelog
Changes:
Adjusted hero spawn strength per wave (will likely require additional adjustment)
Players can't replace a floor item with another of the same type if the floor item is out of cooldown (this is to prevent you from accidentally wasting items)
Punji cooldown now begins after the trap has been triggered, so you don't get a second immediate usage out of it
Slightly reduced item drop rate
Increased number of elevators
Minor UI adjustments [2015.04.27b]
Slightly toned down the "spread" effect of some items[2015.04.27b]
Punji trap is removed when item is replaced on a floor[2015.04.27]
Fixes:
Fetish passive effect wasn't being applied retroactively
Clicking items while item bar was over Hoard could target the Hoard instead[2015.04.27b]
Fixed potential but rare crash involving items and particles[2015.04.27b]
Bomb Codex description was inaccurate[2015.04.27]

notes.title: Update 2015.04.26: Nothing Ventured...
notes.notes:
http://i.imgur.com/u6Dx9Ko.gif
I made an announcement about big upcoming changes last night, thinking that I would hold off a couple more days before updating, but after knocking out a few more big changes and features today, I started thinking, "Well, now I'll either have to hold off for more Extra Beta testing, or I can just bite the bullet and push it all out now." I have opted for the latter.

What's the point of Early Access if I can't majorly screw with everyone's copy of the game whenever the whim strikes anyway?

There are some daunting patch notes below (and they're the abridged version!), but here are the highlights:

New matching mechanics
New item mechanics
A pause feature
A score multiplier that increases over time, but resets when you pause the game
Fear rewrite (fearful heroes will drop out of battles and retreat from your dungeon)
Codex changes (e.g., you can drag the codex around to reposition it now)
Lots of additional fixes and adjustments


Please let me know what you think of the changes, and report any of the inevitable bugs in the discussion forums! Thank you =)!

[Edit: Updated to 2015.04.27 to fix the Bomb description, remove Punji traps on floor item changes, and prevent duplicate usables from being spawned.]

[Edit 2: Updated to 2015.04.27b to fix a rare crash and make some minor adjustments.]

Changelog
Additions:
Ability to pause (spacebar or on-screen button)
Score multiplier that increases over time (up to x1.5), but drops back to x1 when you pause
Hovering ghost icon on fearful characters
Added a comma to the multiplier font, for regions where it replaces a period in denoting decimal places
Added codex icon that can be clicked to open the codex, or dragged/dropped on things to open to a relevant entry

Changes:
Matching mechanics have changed significantly, allowing for vertical slides and multiple slides per move (four, by default)
Item mechanics have changed significantly, making items re-usable with a cooldown, and sorting items into distinct Usable/Deployable/Passive categories
Floors can now have a deployed item, which will automatically be used when appropriate (and pending a cooldown); assigning a new item will replace the old one
Items that are usable on the Hoard no longer target specific tiles; you just click to use them
Calcifier, Bomb, and 'Sploder are no longer usable on floors
Greater Grasp now increases number of slides allowed per move by two
Portable Punji can now be used on floors that already have traps
Calcifier, 'Sploder, and Mit now "spread" their resource types; any Hoard tiles of their type will randomly infect adjacent tiles
Magnet now immediately sucks up all gear and scrap tiles from the Hoard
Bomb now destroys the top four rows of your Hoard; it does not collect tiles, but it is useful for quickly clearing room for another floor
Reduced item drop rate
Items no longer stack
All items have a type: tool, device, potion, relic, explosive, or artifact
Can no longer purchase items
"Shop" floors now decrease cooldowns for specific categories of items (for example, the Alchemist reduces potion cooldowns by 10 seconds)
Can no longer sell items to Fence by dropping them over that floor (doubt anyone was doing this anyway)
Fenced items now refund their full value
Fenced value is now displayed in the "recycle bin" where you fence items
Fearful heroes will now retreat from you dungeon without engaging your minions (they should still trigger traps, however)
Potion effects no longer stack (this prevents a dormant floor--such as the Sanctum--from benefiting from many item cooldown cycles)
Changed the way fatigue is calculated for characters with buffed defense, allowing defense to be re-buffed (this helps offset the effect-stacking change)
Some tutorial revisions
The codex can now be dragged to reposition it on the screen
A number of display and language changes in the Codex
Many other UI changes and adjustments
Fixes:
"Background text" wouldn't always appear on Codex entries (this is the fake text blocks that surround the actual text and images)
Some splash and shard particles were not behaving appropriately
Assassin backstabs were sometimes broken
There was a *very* brief visual glitch when tiles were collected
Smoothed out some tile motion
Icons on popups wouldn't always move smoothly with the popup
Some Hoard effects were not mirrored on the dedicated Hoard view

notes.title: Major Changes Incoming!
notes.notes:
http://i.imgur.com/52HteQN.gif
Last week, I began offering a separate beta build for Tomb of Tyrants; I know that technically the game as a whole is already in beta, but now you can test extra beta features and changes by checking out the "Betas" tab under the game's Preferences in Steam.

It's been a little while since the last main release (a long while compared to previous update gaps that averaged about half a week), and while I'll admit that some of that delay is due to an onslaught of escalating personal obligations, a lot of it is because I've been trying to improve some of the game's core mechanics, which has required a lot of playing and experimenting on my own.

But now you can help! By testing out Extra Beta 2015.04.25 and leaving your feedback (in this thread or with me directly), you can help me polish up or further revamp some of what I've been working on for the last three weeks.

The two biggest things going on here are big changes to matching and item usage.

Matching Changes:
Instead of grabbing entire rows and moving them left/right, you now grab individual pieces, which you can shift left/right or up/down! This works similarly to the old mechanics, where tiles wrap around, but now you can slide columns and even make multiple slides per move (up to 4), giving you much more control over the Hoard; you can target the resources you actually want, more easily set up large matches, and feel really clever when you do!

I feel that this is more engaging than the old mechanic, because it allows you to spend less time matching, prevents deadlock situations, and yet still allows for the tactics you may have grown accustomed to. However, the point of this testing (and, indeed, Early Access in general) is to find out if this is actually really fun and balanced!

Item Changes:
Usable items are now all re-usable with cooldowns. Instead of using items once on a floor, you now deploy them to a floor, and that floor will then re-use the item regularly. Items that affect the Hoard can simply be clicked to used, as they no longer target specific tiles. Items that previously affected either the Hoard or floors have been changed to only affect the Hoard (so no more using bombs on enemies--although some other item may very well be introduced to fill this role later =).

The goal here was to simplify, and you'll see fewer items in general, because you get more out of the items you receive. This should prevent the inventory from becoming cumbersomely cluttered with stacks of items that you feel pressured to find a use for. You can no longer purchase items, but floors that previously sold them now reduce cooldowns for specific classes of items (for example, the Acrid Alchemist reduces all potion cooldowns by 10 seconds).

I plan to push these changes out in a major release in the next couple of days, but I would love to hear more feedback before that happens. In the meantime, I am correcting some glitches, updating a couple of other features, and maybe adding a dash of new content. There are going to be some long patch notes in a few days =).

Thanks again, everyone!

notes.title: Update 2015.04.04: Happy Easter!
notes.notes:
http://i.imgur.com/duOwlBu.gif

I realize this might reach some regions too late to be much of an Easter surprise, but the good news is that you can easily enjoy this secular content (inspired by one of my favorite Easter/whenever films, Monty Python and the Holy Grail) year-round! The new prophecy requires the Balding Bomb and Holy Warriors packs to be completed, as well as the Lupine Lair be constructed.

This floor produces Bloody Bunnies, which are adorable.

I hope you are all having a great holiday/regular weekend!

Ability for floors to require specific items in your inventory at construction time (you can discard the item after you build the floor)

Changes:

notes.title: Update 2015.03.23: Guilty Guildhall
notes.notes:
http://i.imgur.com/81YjDVC.gif

Tonight's content is only sort of new, considering that the Guilty Guildhall is really just a new home for the existing thieves and sneaks. These two characters were the only examples of minions that were unlocked for an early floor by later floors, and I felt this was a bad precedent that would eventually only serve to complicate the build tree. As a result, they have been moved to a new home that requires either the Shady Shop or the Furtive Fence to build.

Also included in this update are a number of requested options (full screen, vsync, UI margin controls, no auto-pause on minimzation), as well as a balance change to production floors and fencing items: these will now deposit resources directly into your stockpile, rather than dropping tiles into the hoard.

This update also makes a lot of changes to UI width requirements; with the margin controls, it is now possible to fit the alternative floor UI and the dedicated hoard view on a 1080p display. If you previously had some overlap between UI elements, things should be a bit roomier now =).

Thanks for all of the reports and suggestions, everyone!

Changelog
Additions:
Guilty Guildhall--produces Thieves (with Camp) and/or Goblin Sneaks (with Grotto)
Full screen option (known bug: if you exit full screen mode, the window will be un-resizable until you restart the application; this is due to an engine bug that I cannot address until I return home next weekend--sorry!)
VSync option (on by default)
UI margin slider (margins are intended for TVs and other displays that require a title-safe region; previously, the maximum region was enforced)
Pause on Focus Loss option (enabled by default; when disabled, the game will not automatically pause when the window looses focus)

Changes:
Adjusted minimum width requirements for resolution scaling
Default margins have been significantly reduced
Production floors and fenced items now send resources directly to your collected stash and not the Hoard
Production floors no longer produce the occasional item
Removed dedicated glossary buttons during gameplay (and alternative codex location option) because these required an extra vertical column of space

Fixes:
In the codex, floors could miscalculate that they were blocked from construction, when only one possible route was blocked--this did not affect whether the floors could actually be built

notes.notes:

It's a boy! As I've mentioned probably too often for official posts, my wife and I had been expecting, and last week, she gave birth right here at home to our first child, Atlas. I finally decided to just make all of the patrolling AI smarter (rather than just predictable), so now patrolling behavior includes some of the hunter logic; minions will attempt to cut off heroes that slip by. I actually rewrote large amounts of AI while making this change, so we may need to keep an eye on its performance.

There are also a number of UI adjustments and improvements, as well as a bunch of groundwork being laid for some upcoming features.

Speaking of which, if you would like to help test some potential major mechanical changes, here's a thread on how you can help: http://steamcommunity.com/app/340360/discussions/0/610575007204564803/

I'm sorry for the relatively huge delay between updates this time (ten whole days!), but things are finally starting to calm back down, so I should be slowly returning to the more regular update regimen I had been keeping up.

notes.title: Update 2015.02.04--Holy Warriors
notes.notes:
http://i.imgur.com/7O6VCMT.gif

First off, the dedicated hoard view is now on by default, and there have been a bunch of UI adjustments to accommodate this at different resolutions. Let me know how you feel about the new layout, because if people seem okay with it, I will probably keep it this way for the foreseeable future, and move on to updating controller support and such.

All of the game's collectible tiles and items have been changed over to the color-swapping system, so you'll notice some palette changes, because they are now drawn in primary colors rather than their final colors. This is the first step toward allowing players to adjust resource colors to suit their preferences or needs (for color-blind players); you can't change the colors yet, but the groundwork is there.

I've also added a new pack of heroes: a Human Paladin, a Human Monk, and a Dwarven Cleric. They all deal holy damage (so your undead and demons should watch out), and the latter two have some healing abilities.

Holy Warriors hero pack (Human Paladin, Human Monk, and Dwarven Cleric)


Changes:
All tiles moved over to color-swapping
Several UI elements have been rearranged (most noticeably, the minimap and meters)


Fixes:
Multipliers weren't rendering on the hoard view
Damage weakness was sometimes not behaving as intended (one point of damage should always get through)
Prophecy messages weren't updating the message log height properly, causing single messages to sometimes render partially off-screen
When watching the surface, champion stars could render over the hoard view
Corrected a few glitches in floor and character graphics

Reintroducing: rituals! Rituals were the original plan for unlocking new content (instead of prophecies), but prophecies are better, so rituals got nixed--pretty much right before Early Access began.

Rituals are target arrangements of tiles, and this update brings rituals back in a different capacity; completing rituals by matching tiles to the ritual's shape will now earn you resource pool size bonuses, so your maximum assets will increase over the course of a game.

I've also added a new leaderboard for tracking players who have completed the most rituals in a single game. Have at it!

Changelog
Additions:
Rituals
Ritual leaderboard
Ability to use items on a floor by dragging them over the minimap

Fixes:
Purchase buttons were not updating position consistently after resource changes
Using a balding bomb would exhaust the entire stack
